newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Birch attacks Labour "arrogance".
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch attacks Labour "arrogance".

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch accused opposition Labour leader Helen Clark of arrogance on Wednesday after she said she would insist on having Labour's Michael Cullen as finance minister in a Labour-led coalition government.

Birch said Clark was wrong to assume the right to dictate to New Zealand First leader Winston Peters and Alliance leader Jim Anderton, whose support she would need to form a government after Saturday's general election.
"Her condescending assumption of superiority over Mr Peters and Mr Anderton is clearly going to cause huge turbulence in trying to put together a left-wing coalition," he said.
The conservative National Party is telling voters a left-wing government would be an unstable "three-headed monster".

Clark says she is confident she can lead a coalition with New Zealand First, with support from the Alliance in areas such as social policy, health and education. Opinion polls suggest the three parties will jointly command a majority of seats.
